newsitem.title: USA: Clinton still opposed to balanced budget law.
newsitem.headline: Clinton still opposed to balanced budget law.

text.p: President Bill Clinton will fight a balanced budget amendment if proposed by Republicans in Congress, Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said in interviews published on Thursday.
"His position has not changed," Rubin told the Washington Post. "We will actively oppose it if it's proposed."

"He's very much in favour of going to a balanced budget but a balanced budget amendment isn't going to cut the deficit by one nickel," Rubin said. "What it does is create a constitutional inflexibility that can be very dangerous."
He made similar comments in an interview published in Thursday's New York Times.
In remarks made on Tuesday, President Clinton appeared to soften his opposition to a balanced budget amendment, which is strongly backed by conservative Republicans.

Clinton had told reporters when asked about the amendment that "I don't believe we need it, but if we have it, it ought to be able to be implemented in a way that actually works and gives the country what it needs to manage a recession."
